definition: Abstraction means a general idea considered apart from concrete things or specific examples.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word abstraction. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know abstraction should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: On the survey, 'the average commuter' is an abstraction - a rider pieced together from thousands of trips that no single passenger ever took.
A notion is a loose idea drifting through someone's head; abstraction goes further, lifting an idea away on purpose from every concrete case.
A concept is a defined idea you could teach, and it often keeps its examples close; an abstraction has been pulled free of examples on purpose - 'justice' with no courtroom in sight.

A generalization is a broad claim built up from a stack of real cases - 'renters move more often than owners' after checking fifty leases. An abstraction is not a claim at all: it is an idea deliberately lifted away from particular cases so it can be studied on its own.

A construct is an idea people deliberately build as a tool - 'grade level,' 'credit score' - and the word advertises that made-ness. An abstraction points the other way: it has been lifted out of real cases, and it can feel discovered rather than assembled.

A theory is an organized explanation meant to predict and to be tested against evidence. An abstraction carries no such duty: it simply names an idea held apart from concrete cases, useful for thinking even when it explains nothing. A theory does work in the world; an abstraction just holds still.

Abstraction means a general idea considered apart from concrete things or specific examples.

'Momentum,' the coach reminded us, 'never scored a point.' You can graph it, argue about it on sports radio, and print it on a whiteboard, but what actually exists is Tuesday's blocked shot and Friday's twelve-point run - momentum is the abstraction we build above those plays.

Abstraction is the exact word because the idea has been considered apart from concrete things: the blocked shot is real and datable, while 'momentum' gathers a hundred such moments into one idea nobody can touch.
And note that an abstraction is not sloppy - it can be defined precisely; it just can't be pointed at.
An abstraction is not a flaw: 'velocity' and 'justice' are abstractions and perfectly precise.
Reach for the word when you mean an idea lifted away, on purpose, from particular cases.
If an idea is unclear because nobody has pinned it down, the word you want is nebulous, this unit's cloud-word - an abstraction can be exact; a nebulous idea never is.

On the first day of geometry, Ms.
Arroyo drew a circle on the board, then apologized for it.
'This is not a circle,' she said.
The circle is an abstraction.' No circle anyone can touch, she explained, has ever been perfect.
Wheels wobble, coins wear down at the rim, and even a careful compass drags and skips.
The circle her students would study all term was the idea itself, pulled free of every wobbling wheel — a form held apart from its examples so it could be reasoned about.
One student objected that something nobody can touch was not worth a semester.
Arroyo asked how engineers could grind a lens or plot an orbit without it.
The idea makes no claims and predicts nothing on its own, she granted.
It simply holds still, so that everything built from it can move.
